purpose: WAVE-3 CENSUS DESIGN CONSTRAINT. Two instruments, two OPPOSITE blind spots, and between them a real file can be invisible to both.

blind_spot_A.instrument: GIT-BASED ENUMERATION -- `git ls-files`, a tracked-corpus walk, anything whose population is 'what git knows' (proof-of-spec-check.py's corpus is built this way and its header says so)
blind_spot_A.blind_to: UNTRACKED-BUT-PRESENT -- these files are NOT IN ITS POPULATION AT ALL
blind_spot_A.\u26d4_CORRECTED_20260827T0336Z: I first labelled this 'filesystem instruments'. WRONG, and wrong in a way that would send a wave-3 seat to the wrong tool. A FILESYSTEM WALK SEES UNTRACKED FILES -- IT IS HOW EVERY ONE OF THEM WAS FOUND TONIGHT. Corrected by 0.8.0_AE_CloudComp~X.
blind_spot_A.the_precise_shape: filesystem walk: SEES the file, cannot tell you its status -- so it counts it as PRESENT/delivered. git enumeration: does not see it at all. THE PAIR IS THE INSTRUMENT: enumerate the filesystem, then test each member with `git ls-files --error-unmatch` and a firing positive control. Neither half classifies anything alone.
blind_spot_A.evidence: 19 untracked .py estate-wide, none gitignored; a certifier's card battery certified 7 cards existing on one device
blind_spot_A.found_by: filesystem enumeration measured AGAINST git -- 0.4.0_DT_ClientPlatform~X's sweep, 0.8.0_AE_CloudComp~X's card-dir check, 1.0.0_SA_CTO~X's two writers, and my own

blind_spot_B.instrument: the dependency graph's CALLS edges (extract_pipeline_cloud.py enrichment)
blind_spot_B.evidence: its own header, verbatim: 'A COMMITTED-BUT-NEVER-DEPLOYED script is invisible to enrichment BY DESIGN.' It parses DEPLOYED BYTES, not repo source.

\u26d4_THE_PAIR_IS_THE_FINDING: The two blind spots run in OPPOSITE directions. A file that is UNTRACKED BUT DEPLOYED is visible to the graph and to a filesystem walk, and invisible to GIT ENUMERATION. A file that is COMMITTED BUT NOT DEPLOYED is visible to git and invisible to the graph. NEITHER INSTRUMENT ALONE SPANS THE POPULATION, and each returns a CLEAN, WELL-FORMED, CORRECTLY-CONTROLLED answer about its own domain while missing the other half.
why_it_bites_precisely_here: Both untracked candidates are the files a deployed-bytes view is most likely blind to. A CLEAN EMPTY RESULT from the graph on those two would be an artifact of the INSTRUMENT'S DOMAIN, not a statement about delegation -- 0.8.0_AE_CloudComp~X's point, and it is the reason a null there must not be read as a negative.
the_caveat_that_survives: UNTRACKED IS NOT UNDEPLOYED. storage_producer.py's own docstring describes an ancestor that RAN and emitted to S3 while never being committed -- precedent for the exact opposite case. So the two sets overlap in an unmeasured way.
wave_3_consequence: A materializer census must declare WHICH PLANE it read -- repo, deployed, or both -- and carry the other plane's blind spot as a stated limit. This is the same shape as the two-plane trigger census (events vs scheduler): a one-plane sweep returns a TRUE, correctly-controlled answer about the WRONG POPULATION.
NOT_a_gate: observation and a design constraint. No remediation authorized, no seat named at fault.
